paper_title: What Does Neuro Mean to Cardio Investigating the Role of Clinical   Specialty Data in Medical LLMs
caption_used: Negative log-probabilities for clinically relevant tokens between baseline MistralV0.2-Base and the same model further fine-tuned on each specialty data. The chart displays six specialty groups along the x-axis (Cardio, Gastro, Infect, Neuro, Obstetrics, Pediatrics), with the y-axis showing negative log probability ranging from approximately -27 to -22. Within each group, the MistralV0.2-Base bar (light blue) consistently shows the highest negative log probability, indicating weaker token predictions at baseline. Among the fine-tuned models, the Gastro-tuned variant achieves the lowest negative log probability across most specialty groups, suggesting strong cross-specialty transfer. Notably, the Infect group shows the largest overall bar heights, with baseline reaching approximately -23.5, while the Cardio group exhibits the smallest spread between baseline and fine-tuned variants at roughly 1.5 units.
model_annotation: This bar chart illustrates the negative log probabilities of clinically relevant tokens for the MistralV0.2-Base model and its variants fine-tuned on six distinct medical specialties—Cardio, Gastro, Infect, Neuro, Obstetrics, and Pediatrics—along the horizontal x-axis labeled “Per-specialty terms.” The vertical y-axis, labeled “Negative log probability,” is scaled linearly from approximately -27 to -22. Within each specialty group, a single light blue bar represents the baseline MistralV0.2-Base model, while six additional bars, each colored differently according to the legend (light beige for Cardio, light orange for Gastro, orange for Infect, dark orange for Neuro, brown for Obstetrics, and dark brown for Pediatrics), represent the respective fine-tuned models. The baseline MistralV0.2-Base bar consistently extends to the lowest value (most negative) on the y-axis, indicating the weakest token predictions among all models for each specialty group. The fine-tuned models show progressively higher (less negative) negative log probabilities compared to the baseline, with the Gastro-tuned model consistently achieving the highest (least negative) values across most specialty groups. The Infect group exhibits the tallest bars overall, with the baseline bar reaching approximately -23.5. The Cardio group shows the smallest vertical spread between the baseline and fine-tuned bars, approximately 1.5 units. The bars are not sorted by value but are presented in the order of the specialty labels on the x-axis. No bars are visually emphasized with shading, bolding, or annotations beyond their color-coded representation in the legend.
